a9d2ba18.ocr_text:
Principle of Operation: Paging is a memory management technique where a process's
logical memory is divided into fixed-size units called pages, and physical memory is
divided into frames of the same size. The operating system maintains a page table to
map logical addresses to physical addresses.

Page Allocation: When a process requests memory, the OS assigns available frames to its
pages. This ensures efficient memory usage while preventing fragmentation issues.

Hardware Support for Paging: The hardware plays a crucial role in paging, including the
Memory Management Unit (MMU), which translates logical addresses into physical
addresses. Additionally, a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) helps improve
performance by storing frequently accessed page mappings.

What are sequences?

Sequences are containers with items that are accessible by indexing or
slicing. The built-in lenQ) function takes any container as an argument and
returns the number of items in the container.

Sequence Operations:

Concatenation - Combine multiple sequences together

Repetition - To repeat particular sequence multiple times

Membership Testing - To check the item is belonging to the particular
seq
